hook: Waiting ten years to invest can cost you almost three hundred thousand dollars.

blocks.narration: Waiting ten years to invest can cost you almost three hundred thousand dollars. Two friends each invest two hundred dollars a month. Maya starts at twenty-five. Jake waits until thirty-five. At a seven percent average return, by sixty-five Maya has about five hundred twenty-five thousand. Jake has about two hundred forty-four thousand. Maya put in just twenty-four thousand more. Start small, start now.
blocks.visual: Two clay friends invest the same monthly amount; the one who starts ten years earlier ends with a coin tower twice as tall

cta: Start small, start now. Follow for one money rule a day.
visual_style: bright 3D clay animation, soft studio light, rounded characters, navy and gold palette

captions.body: $200/month at a hypothetical 7% average annual return, compounded monthly, until 65. Start at 25: about $525k. Start at 35: about $244k. The early starter contributes only $24k more. Time in the market does the heavy lifting.

sources.claim: Compound growth of monthly contributions (FV of $200/mo at 7%, monthly compounding)
